Richard Donner (born Richard Donald Schwartzberg; April 24, 1930 – July 5, 2021) was an American filmmaker. Described as "one of Hollywood's most reliable makers of action blockbusters", Donner directed some of the most financially successful films of the 1970s and 1980s. His career spanning more than six decades crossed genres and influenced trends among filmmakers across the world.

Donner began his career in 1957 as a television director. In the 1960s, he directed episodes of the series The Rifleman, The Man from U.N.C.L.E., The Fugitive, The Twilight Zone, The Banana Splits, and many others.

**Naveen D. Padil** (born 11 November 1969) is an acclaimed Indian theatre and film actor who primarily works in Tulu and Kannada cinema. Widely celebrated in Tulu theatre circles as a master of comedy and tragedy, he is affectionately known by fans as "Kusalda Arase" (The King of Comedy). With a prolific stage career, he has performed in over a thousand plays, leaving an indelible mark on regional theater.

Born in Padil, Mangalore, Karnataka, his deep roots in the coastal region's cultural fabric profoundly influenced his artistic journey.
